$comment: SecondBrainBridge listing for the OpenAI plugin directory (7-section form). Same schema as reminders.openai.config.json (RemindersBridge). This is the Mac Bridge family's first PAID connector: a Free tier plus a Stripe-billed Pro tier. Secrets (reviewer demo password, Stripe keys) are NOT stored here; read from ../.env.local by env var name. PENDING before submit: a hosted demo VIDEO (info.demoRecordingUrl) and the domain-verification token (set OPENAI_APPS_CHALLENGE on Vercel when the MCP section issues it).

info.name: SecondBrainBridge
info.subtitle: Search your Obsidian notes
info.subtitleNote: Subtitle MUST be 30 characters or fewer (OpenAI validates this). This is 26.
info.description: SecondBrainBridge connects ChatGPT to your Obsidian-style Markdown vault — the folder of notes you already keep on your Mac. Ask a question and it retrieves the passages most relevant to it, so ChatGPT answers grounded in your own writing instead of guessing: "What did I decide about Q3?", "Summarize my notes on deep work", "What links to my OKRs note?". Your notes never live on our servers — every search and read happens on your own Mac through a small open-source agent you install with one command (npx second-brain-agent), and the relay only carries each request for the seconds it's in flight. The Free plan covers search, ask, and read (up to 20 searches a day). Pro ($8/mo, billed by Stripe) adds unlimited search, the backlink / knowledge-graph tools, and creating notes from chat — with a cloud multi-source aggregator on the way. Open source (MIT) and self-hostable.
info.developerIdentityNote: Substring matched against the verified identities in the dropdown (Dupree Ops LLC). Identity verification already completed for the earlier Mac Bridge submissions.
info.demoRecordingNote: REQUIRED by OpenAI. YouTube (Unlisted). Demo arc against the reviewer vault: list_sources → search_knowledge (quarter goals) → get_note (OKRs) → backlinks (Pro) → create_note (Pro).
info.commerceNote: LEFT UNCHECKED on the submission form. At review time billing is disabled (no STRIPE_* env set → billingEnabled=false → every account is Pro), so there is no live purchase link-out and the reviewer never encounters a paywall. The optional Pro subscription is sold on the product's own website (/upgrade → Stripe), not through ChatGPT. If Stripe is wired later and in-directory monetization is desired, revisit this — OpenAI's directory only supports physical-good sales, not digital subscriptions, so keep monetization off-platform.

domainVerification.note: The MCP section issues a token you must serve at /.well-known/openai-apps-challenge on the MCP hostname. server/api/challenge.js serves it from the OPENAI_APPS_CHALLENGE env var. Set it on Vercel (`vercel env add OPENAI_APPS_CHALLENGE production`), redeploy, then click Verify Domain. The token is a PUBLIC value, not a secret.

reviewerDemo.note: Reviewers use these to test the app 24/7 with no Mac (demo mode). The account authenticates on the OAuth consent page with email + password; the password lives in ../.env.local, never in this file. Enter the same values verbatim in the Testing section's Test credentials box. The demo account serves a server-side FICTIONAL knowledge vault (isolated per user) and is provisioned as Pro, so every tool works and no real notes are ever exposed. Reviewers can call get_plan to confirm the account shows plan: pro.

prompts: What did I write about deep work?
What links to my OKRs note?
promptsNote: Up to 3 showcase prompts (Prompts section). They render as @Plugin chat bubbles.

testPrompts.prompt: What did I write about deep work?
What links to my OKRs note?

testCases.expected: Returns the demo vault ('Demo Vault', 6 notes) with a per-folder breakdown — Work (3: Q3 Planning, OKRs, Project Atlas), Ideas (1: Deep Work), Recipes (1: Sourdough), and one note at the root (Reading List).

testCases.prompt: Search my notes for quarter goals
testCases.expected: Returns the most relevant passages first — the 'Q3 Planning' note ('Goals for the quarter tie back to our [[OKRs]]…') and the 'OKRs' note (Objective + KR1/KR2/KR3), each with its source path. (The 'ask' tool answers the same way for a natural-language question.)
Returns the full body of Work/OKRs.md — 'Objective: become the default way people bring their own tools into ChatGPT' with KR1 (4 connectors live), KR2 (1,000 weekly active), KR3 ($2k MRR).

testCases.prompt: What links to my Deep Work note?
testCases.expected: A Pro tool; the demo account is Pro so it runs. Returns the notes that wikilink to Deep Work — 'Q3 Planning' (…see [[Deep Work]]) and 'Reading List' (…see [[Deep Work]]) — under linked_from.

testCases.scenario: Create a note from chat (Pro, write, confirmed)
testCases.prompt: Save a note called Ideas Backlog with three connector ideas
testCases.expected: A Pro write tool; ChatGPT confirms the write first, then create_note adds 'Ideas Backlog.md' to the demo vault and returns it. A follow-up search_knowledge for 'Ideas Backlog' then finds it.

testCasesNote: Testing section requires EXACTLY 5 positive test cases; run against the seeded demo vault. The demo account is Pro, so the two Pro tools (backlinks, create_note) are exercisable. Reviewers can also run get_plan to confirm plan: pro and see what Pro unlocks.

negativeTestCases.scenario: A general question about note-taking methods in the abstract — not a request to search or act on the user's own vault. There is nothing to retrieve, so SecondBrainBridge should not trigger.
negativeTestCases.prompt: What's a good method for organizing notes so I can find them later?

negativeTestCases.scenario: The user refers to a different, non-file knowledge tool. SecondBrainBridge works only with the local Obsidian/Markdown vault on the Mac and should not trigger for Notion, Evernote, Roam, or similar.
negativeTestCases.prompt: Add this to my Notion database.

negativeTestCases.scenario: A reminder or calendar action, not a knowledge-vault read or write. SecondBrainBridge searches and writes Markdown notes only; it should not trigger to set a reminder or create a calendar event.
negativeTestCases.prompt: Remind me to review my notes tomorrow at 9am.

negativeTestCasesNote: Testing section requires EXACTLY 3 negative test cases (prompts where the app should NOT trigger).
releaseNotes: Initial release. SecondBrainBridge connects ChatGPT to your Obsidian-style Markdown vault through a small open-source agent that runs on your own Mac — ask a question and it retrieves the passages most relevant to it, reads any note, and maps the [[wikilink]] graph, so ChatGPT answers grounded in your own writing. Your notes never live on our servers; the cloud piece is only a stateless relay. Free covers search, ask, and read (20 searches/day); Pro ($8/mo, via Stripe) adds unlimited search, backlink / knowledge-graph tools, and creating notes from chat. Open source (MIT) and self-hostable.
